consequences.text: In 2016 the US FTC charged that InMobi's SDK, until December 2015, tracked people's locations through nearby Wi-Fi networks even when they had denied apps location access, and collected children's data from child-directed apps without parental consent. Under a court order InMobi had to pay $950,000 of a $4 million penalty and is barred from collecting or inferring location without consent.
consequences.wording: Settled with the US FTC: a court order entered 2016-06-27. InMobi neither admitted nor denied the charges.

consequences.text: A class action alleges that InMobi's SDK, in a dating app, sent a user's precise location, advertising ID, IP address and device details to InMobi without his consent, and that the data was linked to his real-world identity through an identity-resolution service and added to advertising profiles. The court refused to dismiss the case in April 2026; InMobi denies the allegations.

GLEIF's record reports a consolidating parent without an LEI, so it doesn't say who owns InMobi Technology Services Private Limited.
